extracted.intended_audience: college mathematics faculty, assessment practitioners, and mathematics-education researchers interested in quantitative literacy assessment
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and evaluation criteria for designing and interpreting assessment of quantitative literacy in college courses, with example scoring items, program-level measures, and course-level assessment practices (placement tests, midterms, portfolios, reflections, GPA/retention analysis).

rubrics_metrics.name: Holistic A–E rating scale for problem responses
rubrics_metrics.description: Each problem response is rated holistically A–E: A = completely correct; B = basically correct with a minor error; C = flawed response but quite close to a correct solution; D = student took some appropriate action but far short of a solution; E = no response or nothing relevant to the problem.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used as an overall judgment of student understanding; examples show distributions (e.g., Example 1: A or B = 30% overall understanding). Apply to whole-response quality rather than tallying isolated correct steps.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interpretation of graphical information in real-world context
rubrics_metrics.description: Ability to interpret a graph in the context of a real-world situation (e.g., determine production ranges that are profitable, identify x-intercepts and bounds, explain reasoning).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Scoring can include distinct checks such as 'Accurately estimated lower bound (x-intercept)', 'Gave the exact upper bound', and 'Gave a correct written explanation (profitability corresponds to positive function values)'. Example item success rates: 30% estimated lower bound, 40% gave exact upper bound, 35% gave correct written explanation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Locate independent-variable value producing a maximum (from graph)
rubrics_metrics.description: Identify the x-value (not the value of the function) that yields the largest profit (or analogous maximum) as read/estimated from a graph.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Common student error: reporting the maximum function value instead of the x corresponding to the maximum. Example: 'Accurately estimated x value corresponding to maximum' scored 95% while 5% incorrectly stated the maximum profit rather than the number of units.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interpret and compute values from contingency/tabular data
rubrics_metrics.description: Read a two-way table correctly to answer questions like 'How many read Time?', 'How many read neither?', 'How many read at least one?'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Scoring items include 'Selected correct numbers' and 'Gave correct total'; example success rates indicate common partial-credit patterns (e.g., 15% selected correct numbers, 20% gave correct total on one question).

rubrics_metrics.name: Extract key values and times from a time-series graph
rubrics_metrics.description: From a time-series plot (e.g., pulse rate every 15 minutes), estimate highest and lowest values and their occurrence times, estimate average over interval, and identify suspect/anomalous readings with justification.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Acceptable numeric estimation ranges are specified in examples (e.g., highest rate estimates of 97–99 accepted; average estimate range 78–82). Example success rates: 93% estimated highest rate correctly, 87% gave correct time. 'Identified 12:45 reading with some appropriate comment' scored 80%.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compute averages and identify extremes from seasonal/time-slot data
rubrics_metrics.description: Calculate average viewers across seasons/time slots; identify period with fewest households tuned and season with highest average viewers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Scoring checks include 'Selected correct numbers from table', 'Attempted to use correct method to compute average', and 'Gave correct average number'. Example: for Prime time average, 100% selected correct numbers, 93% attempted correct method, 93% gave correct average number. Sometimes attempts to compute unnecessary averages are observed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sketch a possible graph consistent with sign-chart and derivatives
rubrics_metrics.description: Given a sign chart for f, f', and f'', produce an appropriate sketch for different x-intervals and identify intervals where the function is decreasing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Scoring components: 'Appropriate graph for x<–1', 'Appropriate graph for –1<x<1', 'Appropriate graph for x>1', and 'Gave correct interval where f is decreasing'. Example success rates around 63% for many subparts; degree-of-success distribution provided (A 25%, B 37%, C 19%, D 19%).

rubrics_metrics.name: Estimate definite integrals from a graph using numerical methods
rubrics_metrics.description: Estimate the value of an integral from a plotted function using methods such as grid estimation, rectangle rule, trapezoid rule, or Simpson's rule, and provide a reasonable numeric estimate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Scoring considers which numerical method was used and whether the final estimate is reasonable. Example: 'Used grid to estimate area' scored 71%, and 53% 'Gave reasonable estimate'; in example no students reported using rectangles/trapezoid/Simpson in that administration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Modeling with geometry and optimization (cylindrical can problem)
rubrics_metrics.description: Set up relationships (e.g., express h as function of r given fixed volume), derive surface area A(r) including sides and top/bottom, find radius minimizing surface area via derivative, and confirm local minimum.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Scoring broken into subskills: 'Correctly expressed h as function of r' (75%), 'Exhibited rule for area of side and top/bottom', 'Derived function for surface area in terms of r', 'Found derivative', 'Attempted to find zero', 'Found the zero', and 'Confirmed local minimum'. Partial-credit pattern visible (high for setup, lower for full optimization); degree-of-success distribution provided (A 6%, B 25%, C 25%, D 44%).

rubrics_metrics.name: Estimate derivatives from a graph and determine sign intervals
rubrics_metrics.description: Estimate f'(x) at specific x-values (e.g., f'(4), f'(2)) and determine intervals where f'(x) < 0 from the graph.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evidence of multiple acceptable approaches: sketching tangent (not necessary), commenting on local minima/horizontal tangent, or estimating slope ranges (e.g., at x=2 estimate –3 < m < –1). Scoring includes observed behaviors and correct interval identification; example success rates vary (e.g., degree of success A 56%, B 31%, C 13%).

rubrics_metrics.name: Design principle: tailor instruments to discipline-specific quantitative requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Quantitative literacy is defined relative to an individual's chosen profession or program of study; therefore assessment instruments should be tailored to reflect the quantitative requirements of particular settings rather than a single universal instrument.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rationale: tailored instruments provide better insight across a broad range of students, avoid triviality for technical backgrounds, and are more collaborative/faculty-driven. The paper endorses multiple instruments rather than one test.

rubrics_metrics.name: Feedback loop targeted to course instructor and collaborative follow-up
rubrics_metrics.description: After exam results compilation, initial feedback is given to the instructor of the course in which the test was administered (not to prerequisite instructors), focusing on identifying significance of low performance and examining student records (grades in prerequisites).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The feedback loop is flexible and collaborative — after initial analysis, course instructor and assessment team decide remedial or curricular actions. Examples illustrate scenarios (weak background vs. disparity in grading or non-persistence of short-term skills).

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of placement exam (COMPASS) for identifying students for remediation
rubrics_metrics.description: Employ a standardized placement instrument (COMPASS) to identify students with significant quantitative deficiencies for placement into remedial/problem-solving courses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Practical notes: between 10%–15% place into QPS; watch for false positives (students placed into QPS though GPA/courses/SAT suggest otherwise). Placement exam provides subcategory scores useful for diagnosis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Midterm and final assessments focused on course content to measure student growth
rubrics_metrics.description: Use midterm and final assessments that resemble in-class problems to detect student growth areas and identify items needing instructional attention; because course is pass/fail, these assessments function diagnostically.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Observed scoring pattern: approximately 60% completely correct, 25% specific technical mistakes, 15% other; use results to identify recurrent errors and inform instruction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transfer-of-method assessment (novel problem transfer)
rubrics_metrics.description: Assess students' ability to transfer solution methods from a known context to a novel context (e.g., 'Roads to War' problem to medical treatment analogy).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design a problem that requires applying the same method in a different context; in example, 60% successfully transferred method (focus multiple lower-intensity rays). Use correctness of method transfer as explicit scoring criterion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Written reflections as evidence of learning and metacognition
rubrics_metrics.description: Require students to write personal reflections on what they learned, their problem-solving strategies, and perceived benefits or limitations of the course.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reflections provide qualitative insight into students' perceptions (e.g., valuing making themselves figure things out, usefulness of computer modules, confidence with word problems). Use samples to triangulate learning outcomes and course improvements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Faculty journal for cross-section consistency and identifying problem difficulty
rubrics_metrics.description: Instructors keep a journal recording daily activities, interesting student responses, emergent questions, and attendance to provide consistency across sections and surface recurring student issues.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Journal useful early for identifying problems and skills needing attention; effectiveness may decline as problem sets standardize (the paper notes journals were not kept in later years).

rubrics_metrics.name: Anecdotal and observational follow-up as qualitative outcome evidence
rubrics_metrics.description: Collect anecdotal stories and observations of former students in subsequent courses to assess longer-term application of skills learned (e.g., students demonstrating group management or detailed solutions later).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These are qualitative data points that can corroborate other measures; use sparingly and as supporting evidence rather than primary evaluation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Institutional outcome measures: GPA and retention comparisons
rubrics_metrics.description: Compare GPA and retention rates across students who tested into QPS, those who took/completed QPS, those who tested out, and those who did not take the course to evaluate broader institutional impact.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example results: students who tested out had GPA 2.58 and retention 77%; those who completed QPS had GPA 2.02 and retention 67%; failing or not taking QPS had GPA 1.65 and retention 57%. Use statistical testing (reported significance at .05) and note sample-size caveats and selection effects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pre- and post-test measurement with subcategory diagnostics
rubrics_metrics.description: Administer the placement test (COMPASS) as both pre- and post-test to measure change; examine subcategory scores (pre-algebra, basic arithmetic, miscellaneous) to diagnose where improvement occurred or did not.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: only 46% tested out after taking the course; students who failed post-test showed pre- and post-subcategory scores that did not improve, suggesting persistent deficiencies. Compare subcategory trajectories across groups for deeper diagnosis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Student-constructed portfolio of problems and solutions as assessment artifact
rubrics_metrics.description: Have students assemble a portfolio of solved problems over the semester (their 'own reference text') to demonstrate problem-solving processes and growth.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Portfolios act as both learning artifacts and assessment evidence; instructors used them alongside class activities and computer review modules to motivate sustained engagement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of computer review modules and external materials as instructional/assessment supports
rubrics_metrics.description: Require students to complete out-of-class review modules (e.g., Introductory Algebra Software) to refresh arithmetic/algebra skills, allowing in-class time to focus on problem-solving in context.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Student feedback indicates modules effectively reviewed basic skills and aided applications; include module completion and resulting performance as part of assessment triangulation.
